liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Lazy Lightning** (1 review): Reviewer loves the Lazy Lightning into Supplication, especially Bobby's vocal line about getting high [31]
- **Dancin' In The Streets** (1 review): Reviewer finds goofy pseudo-disco feel in Dancin' and Lazy Lightning [35]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (1 review): Reviewer calls the Scarlet>Fire great and worth having the show for alone [35]
- **Saint Stephen** (1 review): Reviewer calls the St Stephen wimpy and little more than filler [35]
- **Morning Dew** (1 review): Reviewer says the Morning Dew performance gives chills [24]

## The recordings

- **gd1977-05-08.sbd.cantor.sacks.266.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 20 songs; 205 min; rated 4.72/5 by 36 [1]
- **gd77-05-08.sbd.hicks.4982.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 180 min; rated 4.64/5 by 300 [2]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls the soundboard impeccable, better than most or all official Dead live releases; Reviewer calls it probably the best-sounding Dead soundboard recording you will hear; Reviewer praises Phil's bass, with bombs crashing everywhere in the recording [26][27][31][32]
- **gd1977-05-08.mtx.seamons.97274.sbeok.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 177 min; rated 4/5 by 18 [6]. Said about its sound: Uploader says the ten-foot-from-stage tape has great instrument pickup but vocals a bit lower than Moore's copy [6]
- **gd1977-05-08.148737.SBD.Betty.Anon.Noel.t-flac2448**: soundboard; 20 songs; 179 min; rated 4/5 by 4 [7]

## Around the show

- Tape flips occur after Supplication and during Not Fade Away, causing a few pauses [6]
- Reviewer says every second-set song is at least a top-10 version, though better individual versions exist elsewhere [26]
- Reviewer prefers the previous night's setlist but considers this the best-sounding Dead soundboard [27]
- Reviewer says it is overshadowed by 5-7, 6-9 and 9-3-77, and the first set is unremarkable apart from its closer [30]
- Reviewer disputes Dick Latava's view that the show is overrated, noting he says the same of 27/08/72 [31]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1977-05-08.sbd.cantor.sacks.266.shnf**: taped by Betty Cantor; transferred by Darrin Sacks; source: WBOTB Source -- 7" two track BBD reel encoded w/ DBX-1 noise reduction @ 7 1/2 ips > Sony PCM501ES @ 44.055 kHz. Sony PCM501ES analog out > DBX-1 decoder >… [1]. Also: Audience splices came from a Panasonic AM/FM stereo boom box with condenser mics, onto cassette master, then equalized and edited to CD [1]
- **gd77-05-08.sbd.hicks.4982.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Steve Maizner; transferred by Rob Eaton; source: Matrix (see notes) [2]. Also: Reviewer says this was one of the earliest-released great soundboards, hence its large following; Reviewer claims no soundboard exists because the band forgot to tape it; says good audience tapes exist; Betty Board from 7-inch Nagra half-track reels at 7.5ips, transferred via Sony PCM 501; Rob Eaton remastered with audience splices [2][30][34]
- **gd1977-05-08.mtx.seamons.97274.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Hunter Seamons; source: Matrix mix (SBD/AUD) [6]. Also: Matrix combines the Betty Board with handheld Shure 57 audience recording made ten feet from the stage [6]
- **gd1977-05-08.148737.SBD.Betty.Anon.Noel.t-flac2448**: taped by Betty Cantor; transferred by Source & Transfer by Anonymous;Edited & Mastered using Adobe Audition by Joe Noel; source: Source: Betty Cantor's SBD Reel Master > PCM (undecoded) > DAT via spdif/Sony PCM601esd > wav file via spdif/RME multiface > Wave 24/48 (decoded) > Myteck… [7]. Also: Source shared anonymously; dusborne did the matrix work [7]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Jay Maybrey: [Celebrate the legendary Grateful Dead show at Barton Hall, performed 48 years ago today](https://nysmusic.com/2025/05/08/celebrate-the-legendary-grateful-dead-show-at-barton-hall-performed-43-years-ago-today/) [38]
- Poster by arizjones.blogspot.com: [Grateful Dead, Barton Hall, Cornell University, Ithaca, New York, 5-08-1977](https://arizjones.blogspot.com/2015/06/grateful-dead-barton-hall-cornell.html) [39]
- Poster by Mabrey: [1977 Grateful Dead Cornell Concert Poster](https://www.icollector.com/1977-Grateful-Dead-Cornell-Concert-Poster_i8463417) [40]
- Fan art by blackmuddyblog.blogspot.com: [Grateful Dead - 1977-05-08 - Barton Hall, Cornell University, Ithaca NY (Get Shown The Light, Part II)](https://blackmuddyblog.blogspot.com/2017/05/grateful-dead-1977-05-08-barton-hall.html) [41]
- Poster by thecurtainwithblog.blogspot.com: [Grateful Dead - 1977-05-08 Barton Hall Cornell University Ithaca, NY](https://thecurtainwithblog.blogspot.com/2017/02/grateful-dead-1978-05-08-barton-hall.html) [42]
- Poster by Luke Z. Fenchel: [Revisiting The Grateful Dead's 1977 Barton Hall show](https://www.ithaca.com/news/local_news/revisiting-the-grateful-deads-1977-barton-hall-show/article_9bc4474d-7463-5140-9b7c-7df7bb1b0264.html) [43]

claims.text: Reviewer says the Morning Dew performance gives chills
Reviewer calls the soundboard impeccable, better than most or all official Dead live releases
Reviewer says every second-set song is at least a top-10 version, though better individual versions exist elsewhere
Reviewer prefers the previous night's setlist but considers this the best-sounding Dead soundboard
Reviewer calls it probably the best-sounding Dead soundboard recording you will hear
Reviewer says it is overshadowed by 5-7, 6-9 and 9-3-77, and the first set is unremarkable apart from its closer
Reviewer says this was one of the earliest-released great soundboards, hence its large following
Reviewer loves the Lazy Lightning into Supplication, especially Bobby's vocal line about getting high
Reviewer praises Phil's bass, with bombs crashing everywhere in the recording
Reviewer disputes Dick Latava's view that the show is overrated, noting he says the same of 27/08/72
Reviewer says the show's hype comes from all-time best versions of Scarlet/Fire, Morning Dew and Dancin'
Reviewer says the remaster sounds better than ever
Reviewer claims no soundboard exists because the band forgot to tape it; says good audience tapes exist
Reviewer calls the Scarlet>Fire great and worth having the show for alone
Reviewer finds goofy pseudo-disco feel in Dancin' and Lazy Lightning
Reviewer calls the St Stephen wimpy and little more than filler
Audience splices came from a Panasonic AM/FM stereo boom box with condenser mics, onto cassette master, then equalized and edited to CD
Betty Board from 7-inch Nagra half-track reels at 7.5ips, transferred via Sony PCM 501; Rob Eaton remastered with audience splices
Matrix combines the Betty Board with handheld Shure 57 audience recording made ten feet from the stage
Uploader says the ten-foot-from-stage tape has great instrument pickup but vocals a bit lower than Moore's copy
Tape flips occur after Supplication and during Not Fade Away, causing a few pauses
Source shared anonymously; dusborne did the matrix work
